full_judgment:
27. On behalf of opposite party No.1 a counter affidavit has been filed stating that the detenu was engaged in prejudicial activities by breaking the order of Emergency and violating law, so the opposite party had no other alternative but to prevent him from doing prejudicial activities and the order of detention was rightly passed for the internal security, peace and maintenance of law and order and the economic interest of the country. It has further been stated that before the issuance of the order of detention all the legal requirements and formalities were followed and sufficient materials were placed before it for its satisfaction to pass the order of detention against the detenu. The detenu is a former member of the parliament from Dhaka-12 and is an active member of Bangladesh Awami League and behind the political activities the detenu and his associates constitute a threat to the internal security of Bangladesh and is likely to endanger public safety and maintenance of public order. A supplementary counter affidavit has been filed annexing copy of a report dated 10.2.2007 from the Zonal Officer, Pallabi Zone, Dhaka to special police Super, City Special Branch, Dhaka, a forwarding letter submitted to the Assistant Police Super (B-5) City S.B. Dhaka dated 10.2.2007 in respect of Mirpur P.S. Case No. 92 dated 30.8.2006 filed against the detenu under section 143/341/353/427 and 114 of the Penal Code and the copy of a G.D. entry dated 12.6.2007. A perusal of the G.D. entry shows that the same was lodged by the Officer-in-Charge Gulshan Police Station stating some facts wildly having no particulars and also mentioning of some specific cases as mentioned in the grounds of detention. We have also seen the secret file produced before us and on perusal of the same we found no material other than said police report filed on 10.2.2007 which is a post dated one which prima-facie show that the Government had no materials whatsoever for its objective satisfaction that the activities of the detenu were prejudicial within the meaning of clause (f) of Section 2 of the Act. Mere using of some strong words in the order or grounds of detention shall not construe prejudicial activities but there must be materials to construe the activities of the detenu to be prejudicial. It is by now also a settled proposition that past activities of a person cannot be a ground for justifying an order of detention to be legal or proper. For the discussions made above we are constrained to hold that the detenu Kamal Ahmed Majumder is being detained in custody illegally and improperly. 

 32. From the grounds of detention which were served upon the detenu on 20.1.2007 it appears that in grounds (Ka) and (ga) some vague allegations have been made and in ground (Kha) specific a specify case being Dhanmondi police station Case No. 13 dated 12.3.2004 under section 143/147/447/323/ 379/109/506 of the Penal Code has been mentioned.
